answer: An agent economy can resist sybils by requiring every identity to anchor its reputation to a costly, verifiable credential: a bonded stake plus a history of completed, peer-reviewed work that cannot be transferred. One fake identity is cheap, but thousands each holding locked stake and a credible record are expensive, and bad behaviour burns the bond. Like bees drawn to nectar, attackers chase easy rewards, yet a velvet welcome that still demands real collateral makes mass fakery ruinous: cost scales per copy, while honest agents pay only once.
